`maxAutoGrowHeight={200}` hardcodes a magic number. Every other `maxAutoGrowHeight` usage in the codebase references a named value from `variables` (e.g. `variables.textInputAutoGrowMaxHeight`), which keeps input sizing consistent and themeable. A bare `200` is undocumented and diverges from that convention.

Use the shared style variable instead of an inline literal:

```tsx
import variables from '@styles/variables';

<TextInput
    // ...
    autoGrowHeight
    maxAutoGrowHeight={variables.textInputAutoGrowMaxHeight}
/>
```

If this input genuinely needs a taller max height than the shared value, add a named constant in `variables.ts` (e.g. `searchNLFilterMaxHeight`) and reference it here.

The `capture_method` attribute is stamped with the raw string literals `'photo'` and `'snapshot'`. These are meaningful domain values (they mirror the `takePhoto` vs `takeSnapshot` branch in `captureReceipt`) but are hardcoded inline with no constant or comment, unlike every telemetry attribute *key* which this PR defines in `CONST.TELEMETRY`. Undocumented magic strings like these can silently drift out of sync with the capture logic and the dashboards that read them.

Define the values as named constants alongside the other telemetry constants and reference them here, e.g.:

```ts
// in CONST.TELEMETRY
CAPTURE_METHOD_PHOTO: 'photo',
CAPTURE_METHOD_SNAPSHOT: 'snapshot',
```

```ts
[CONST.TELEMETRY.ATTRIBUTE_CAPTURE_METHOD]: isFlashUsed || isInLandscapeMode ? CONST.TELEMETRY.CAPTURE_METHOD_PHOTO : CONST.TELEMETRY.CAPTURE_METHOD_SNAPSHOT,
```

This line replaces the named reference `variables.sectionMargin` with a hardcoded magic number `16`. The value `16` is not self-explanatory in this context and is no longer tied to any documented constant, so a future reader cannot tell whether it is intentionally decoupled from `sectionMargin` (now `20`) or an oversight. Since `sectionMargin` was intentionally bumped to `20`, hardcoding `16` here silently freezes the old spacing without explanation.

Introduce a named constant for the chart header spacing (or reuse an existing one that semantically represents this value) instead of a bare literal:

```ts
// in variables.ts
chartHeaderMargin: 16,

// in index.ts chartHeader
marginBottom: variables.chartHeaderMargin,
```

If the intent is truly to keep the pre-bump spacing, add a comment explaining why this section must stay at 16 while `sectionMargin` is 20.

The `Exclude<ValueOf<typeof CONST.BUTTON_SIZE>, 'small'>` type hardcodes the string literal `'small'` instead of the already-imported named constant `CONST.BUTTON_SIZE.SMALL`. Referencing the literal duplicates the const value and will not stay in sync if the constant changes.

Reference the constant instead:

```ts
size?: Exclude<ValueOf<typeof CONST.BUTTON_SIZE>, typeof CONST.BUTTON_SIZE.SMALL>;
```

The `Exclude<ValueOf<typeof CONST.BUTTON_SIZE>, 'small'>` type hardcodes the string literal `'small'` rather than the existing named constant `CONST.BUTTON_SIZE.SMALL`. Using the raw literal couples the type to the const value and will drift silently if that value changes.

Reference the constant instead:

```ts
size?: Exclude<ValueOf<typeof CONST.BUTTON_SIZE>, typeof CONST.BUTTON_SIZE.SMALL>;
```

The `Exclude<ValueOf<typeof CONST.BUTTON_SIZE>, 'small'>` type hardcodes the string literal `'small'`. This value is already defined as the named constant `CONST.BUTTON_SIZE.SMALL`, so duplicating the raw literal couples this type to the const's value: if `CONST.BUTTON_SIZE.SMALL` ever changed, the `Exclude` would silently stop excluding the intended member.

Reference the constant instead:

```ts
size?: Exclude<ValueOf<typeof CONST.BUTTON_SIZE>, typeof CONST.BUTTON_SIZE.SMALL>;
```

The `fitPolicy={2}` value is a magic number. The `react-native-pdf` fit-policy enum (`0` = fit width, `1` = fit height, `2` = fit both) is not self-explanatory from the digit alone, and the reason for switching from `1` to `2` (fitting the full landscape page) is not obvious to future readers.

Define a named constant for the fit-policy values (e.g. in `CONST.ts` or alongside `PDFThumbnailProps`) and reference it here so the intent is clear:

```tsx
// e.g. CONST.PDF_FIT_POLICY.FIT_BOTH = 2
<PDFThumbnail
    fitPolicy={CONST.PDF_FIT_POLICY.FIT_BOTH}
    ...
/>
```

Alternatively, add a brief comment explaining what `2` means and why it is needed here.

The new `data-copyable-text` attribute is introduced as a magic string. The existing SelectionScraper attributes follow the opposite convention — they are defined once in `CONST` (`CONST.SELECTION_SCRAPER_HIDDEN_ELEMENT`, `CONST.INNER_BOX_SHADOW_ELEMENT`) and referenced by name — but this PR hardcodes the raw selector/key (`'[data-copyable-text=true]'` here and in `SelectionScraper/index.ts`, plus `{copyableText: true}` in many components). This makes the DOM contract easy to break (a typo in one spot silently disables copy).

Define the attribute name once in `CONST/index.ts` (next to `SELECTION_SCRAPER_HIDDEN_ELEMENT`), e.g. `COPYABLE_TEXT_ELEMENT: 'copyable-text'`, and derive both the selector and the `dataSet` key (`{[CONST.COPYABLE_TEXT_ELEMENT]: true}` / `` `[data-${CONST.COPYABLE_TEXT_ELEMENT}=true]` ``) from it everywhere.

The `0.001` passed to `addSkipTimeTagToURL` is a magic number with no explanation here. Its meaning (skipping the first millisecond of the video so a preview frame renders while paused) is only clear from the comment that exists in `BaseVideoPlayer.tsx`, which is not present at this call site.

Replace it with a named/documented constant so the intent is self-evident and shared:

```ts
// e.g. in @components/VideoPlayer/utils.ts or CONST
const VIDEO_SKIP_TIME_SECONDS = 0.001; // skip first millisecond so a preview frame shows when paused
```

Then reference `VIDEO_SKIP_TIME_SECONDS` instead of the literal `0.001` in both this component and `BaseVideoPlayer.tsx`.

The new `VIOLATIONS_BY_SUBMITTER` suggested search hardcodes `limit: '10'` as a magic value. Every sibling top/insights search (`TOP_SPENDERS`, `TOP_CATEGORIES`, `TOP_MERCHANTS`) already uses the named constant `CONST.SEARCH.TOP_SEARCH_LIMIT` (which is `10`) for the same "top N" behavior, so inlining `'10'` here duplicates that value and obscures its meaning. If this ever needs to change, the two sources will drift.

Reuse the existing constant instead of a literal:

```ts
// import/reference the shared constant used by the other top searches
limit: String(CONST.SEARCH.TOP_SEARCH_LIMIT),
```

This entry hardcodes the feed prefix `'vcfanzfav'` and the display name `'ANZ NZ'` as inline string literals, while every sibling entry in `COMMERCIAL_FEED_DISPLAY_BASES` references named constants (`CONST.COMPANY_CARD.FEED_BANK_NAME.AMEX/VISA/MASTER_CARD`) and derives its display name via `getBankName`. There is no `vcfanzfav`/ANZ constant anywhere in `CONST`, so this magic string is undocumented and inconsistent with the established convention in this file (feed prefixes live in `CONST.COMPANY_CARD.FEED_BANK_NAME` and display names in `CONST.COMPANY_CARDS.BANKS`/`CARD_TYPE_NAMES`).

Add an ANZ NZ feed prefix constant (e.g. `ANZ_NZ: 'vcfanzfav'`) to `CONST.COMPANY_CARD.FEED_BANK_NAME` and a matching display name constant to `CONST.COMPANY_CARDS.BANKS`, then reference them here:

```ts
{base: CONST.COMPANY_CARD.FEED_BANK_NAME.ANZ_NZ, displayName: CONST.COMPANY_CARDS.BANKS.ANZ_NZ, shouldHideOne: false},
```

The date format string `'MMMM do, yyyy'` is hardcoded. This exact value already exists as a named constant `CONST.DATE.MONTH_DAY_YEAR_ORDINAL_FORMAT` (defined in `src/CONST/index.ts`), and this file consistently references `CONST.DATE.*FORMAT` constants elsewhere (e.g. `MONTH_DAY_YEAR_ABBR_FORMAT`, `LOCAL_TIME_FORMAT`). Using the raw literal risks divergence if the format ever changes.

Replace the literal with the existing constant:

```ts
return formatInTimeZoneWithFallback(date, timeZone, CONST.DATE.MONTH_DAY_YEAR_ORDINAL_FORMAT);
```

The string `'card'` is used as a magic value to distinguish the `origination` of the travel nudge. Its sibling `travelType` values are compared against the shared `CONST.RESERVATION_TYPE` enum, but `origination` (`'manual' | 'card'`) has no named constant, so the intent of the bare literal is only clear if you cross-reference the type definition in `OriginalMessage.ts`.

Consider defining these values as a `CONST` (e.g. `CONST.TRAVEL_NUDGE.ORIGINATION.CARD` / `.MANUAL`) and referencing them both here and in the `OriginalMessageTravelNudge` type:

```ts
const isCardCreated = originalMessage.origination === CONST.TRAVEL_NUDGE.ORIGINATION.CARD;
```

The bare empty string `''` is used as a magic sentinel for the "deselected / cleared" vendor value. It is not self-explanatory and is inconsistent with the sibling changes in this PR (QBO and QBD) which use the named constant `CONST.INTEGRATION_ENTITY_MAP_TYPES.NONE` for the identical "cleared vendor" concept.

Replace the literal with a named/documented value, e.g.:

```tsx
const newValue = value === config?.defaultVendor ? CONST.INTEGRATION_ENTITY_MAP_TYPES.NONE : value;
```

or extract a clearly-named constant documenting that `''` means "no default vendor" if the NetSuite backend requires the empty string.

The bare empty string `''` is used as a magic sentinel to represent the "deselected / cleared" vendor. It is not self-explanatory and is inconsistent with the sibling changes in this PR (QBO and QBD) which use the named constant `CONST.INTEGRATION_ENTITY_MAP_TYPES.NONE` for the same concept.

Replace the literal with a named/documented value, e.g.:

```tsx
const newValue = value === defaultVendor ? CONST.INTEGRATION_ENTITY_MAP_TYPES.NONE : value;
```

or extract a clearly-named constant documenting that `''` means "no default vendor" if the empty string is what the Sage Intacct backend expects.

The bare empty string `''` is used as a magic sentinel to represent "no vendor / deselected". It is not self-explanatory and it is inconsistent with the sibling changes in this same PR (QBO and QBD) which use the named constant `CONST.INTEGRATION_ENTITY_MAP_TYPES.NONE` for the identical "cleared vendor" concept.

Use a named/documented value instead of the bare literal, e.g.:

```tsx
const newValue = row.value === exportConfig?.vendorAccount ? CONST.INTEGRATION_ENTITY_MAP_TYPES.NONE : row.value;
```

or, if the backend requires an empty string here, extract a clearly-named constant documenting that `''` means "no default vendor".

`validateCodeActionErrorField="walletPhoneNumber"` is a hardcoded magic string duplicated from `AdditionalDetailsStep.tsx` and defined as a constant nowhere. A typo in either usage would silently break the error-field wiring.

Extract it to a shared named constant and reference it in both flows instead of repeating the literal.

`validateCodeActionErrorField="walletPhoneNumber"` is a hardcoded magic string. This field key is not defined as a named constant anywhere and is repeated in `PersonalInfo.tsx` too, so a typo in either place would silently break error display and go unnoticed.

Define it as a shared constant (e.g. `CONST.WALLET.VALIDATE_CODE_ERROR_FIELD` or an existing `INPUT_IDS` entry) and reference it in both files:

```tsx
validateCodeActionErrorField={CONST.WALLET.VALIDATE_CODE_ERROR_FIELD}
```

The new `gap24` key has value `gap: 96`, which is misleading and breaks the established naming convention in this file. Every other `gap<N>` entry follows `value = 4 * N` (e.g. `gap6: {gap: 24}`, `gap8: {gap: 32}`), so `gap24` reads as a `24`px gap while it is actually `96`px. There is also already a `gap6` that produces `24`. A future maintainer will very likely misuse it.

Rename it to match the convention so the name reflects the value, e.g.:
```ts
gap24: {
    gap: 96,
},
```
should become something like `gap96: {gap: 96}` (or reuse an existing token if 96 is not actually intended).

The positioning offsets `8` and `4` are magic numbers with no explanation of why these specific pixel values were chosen for the copy button placement. This reduces readability and makes future adjustments error-prone. Note these spacing values also typically map to named tokens in `variables`/the style system rather than raw pixels.

Extract them into named constants or use existing spacing tokens from `variables`/`styles`, e.g.:

```tsx
const COPY_BUTTON_OFFSET_MULTILINE = 8;
const COPY_BUTTON_OFFSET_SINGLELINE = 4;
```

or better, define the corresponding positioned styles in the shared style system.

The noun `'currency'` is introduced as a bare magic string in the `SpendRulePhraseNoun` union (and passed as a literal argument to `getDiffPhrases` on the two new currency phrase blocks). The sibling nouns are referenced through the established named-constant convention `CONST.SPEND_RULES.NOUN.MERCHANT` / `CONST.SPEND_RULES.NOUN.SPEND_CATEGORY` (defined in `src/CONST/index.ts`). A loose literal here diverges from that convention and is not self-explanatory.

Add `CURRENCY: 'currency'` to `CONST.SPEND_RULES.NOUN` and reference it instead:

```ts
type SpendRulePhraseNoun =
    | typeof CONST.SPEND_RULES.NOUN.MERCHANT
    | typeof CONST.SPEND_RULES.NOUN.SPEND_CATEGORY
    | typeof CONST.SPEND_RULES.NOUN.CURRENCY;
```

and pass `CONST.SPEND_RULES.NOUN.CURRENCY` (not `'currency'`) to the two `getDiffPhrases(...)` calls.

This line divides by the raw literal `60000` to convert milliseconds to minutes for `sessionDurationMinutes`. Every other timing value in this file is extracted into a documented, named constant (`SAMPLE_INTERVAL_MS`, `STALE_HEARTBEAT_MS`, `MAX_SAMPLES`, `BYTES_PER_MB`), so this inline literal is inconsistent with the file's own convention and is undocumented.

Extract it into a named constant alongside the others, e.g.:

```ts
const MS_PER_MINUTE = 60 * 1000;
// ...
sessionDurationMinutes: Math.round((record.lastHeartbeat - record.startedAt) / MS_PER_MINUTE),
```

`top: VictoryTheme.axis.padding.top + 8` uses an undocumented magic number `8` for the extra top padding. Its purpose is not self-evident.

Extract it to a named constant (or add it to `VictoryTheme.axis`) so its intent is clear and it can be reused/tuned in one place, e.g.:
```ts
const CHART_TOP_PADDING_EXTRA = 8;
// ...
top: VictoryTheme.axis.padding.top + CHART_TOP_PADDING_EXTRA,
```

The hardcoded fallback translation key `'workspace.common.rules'` is a magic string. It is not self-explanatory as a generic fallback, and it is also a latent correctness bug: if a selected `part` has no matching `FEATURE_ROWS` entry, that feature is mislabeled as "Rules" rather than reflecting the real feature. A `Part` should always have a label, so this arbitrary fallback hides a gap rather than handling it meaningfully.

Consider filtering out parts that have no `labelKey` instead of substituting an unrelated key, e.g.:

```tsx
const controlOnlyFeatures = formatList(
    getControlOnlySelectedParts(targetPolicies, parts)
        .map((part) => FEATURE_ROWS.find((row) => row.part === part)?.labelKey)
        .filter((labelKey): labelKey is TranslationPaths => !!labelKey)
        .map((labelKey) => translate(labelKey)),
);
```

This avoids the magic key and guarantees the rendered feature names are accurate.

Control flow here is driven by comparing `status.actionKey` against the hardcoded translation-path string `'walletPage.bankAccountStatus.unlock'`. Encoding behavior selection via a magic string literal is fragile — if that translation key is ever renamed, the unlock handler silently stops being wired up with no compile error.

Drive this off an explicit field on the status object instead of a string match, e.g. add `requiresUnlockHandler?: boolean` (or a discriminant `action: 'unlock' | 'finish' | ...`) to `BankAccountConnectionStatus` in `getBankAccountConnectionStatus`, and check `status.requiresUnlockHandler ? (onUnlockPress ?? onActionPress) : onActionPress`.

The growl duration `6000` is a hardcoded magic number with no explanation. The codebase already defines growl durations as named constants (`CONST.GROWL.DURATION = 2000`, `CONST.GROWL.DURATION_LONG = 3500`), so introducing a bare `6000` here is inconsistent and unclear about why 6 seconds was chosen for the "View" action growl.

Add a named constant (e.g. `CONST.GROWL.DURATION_WITH_ACTION = 6000`) and reference it:
```ts
Growl.success(growlMessage, CONST.GROWL.DURATION_WITH_ACTION, {label: translateLocal('common.view'), onPress: navigateToExpenseRHP});
```

The array `['Approved', 'Submitted']` uses hardcoded magic strings. These should reference named constants.

If a `CONST.CERTINIA_REPORT_EXPORT_STATUS` is added as suggested, this line becomes:
```ts
const REPORT_EXPORT_STATUSES = Object.values(CONST.CERTINIA_REPORT_EXPORT_STATUS);
```

The string literals `'Approved'` and `'Submitted'` are used as raw magic values here and in several other files (`src/libs/API/types.ts`, `src/libs/actions/connections/FinancialForce.ts`, `CertiniaReportExportStatusPage.tsx`). Since these represent a distinct set of report export statuses (different from the existing `CERTINIA_EXPORT_STATUS` values which are uppercase), they should be defined as named constants in `CONST`.

Add a new constant group in `src/CONST/index.ts`:
```ts
CERTINIA_REPORT_EXPORT_STATUS: {
    APPROVED: 'Approved',
    SUBMITTED: 'Submitted',
},
```
Then use `typeof CONST.CERTINIA_REPORT_EXPORT_STATUS.APPROVED | typeof CONST.CERTINIA_REPORT_EXPORT_STATUS.SUBMITTED` for the type, and reference these constants everywhere instead of bare string literals.

The `emptyStateIllustrationStyle` object is created as an inline style with raw values (`width: '100%' as const`, `maxWidth`, `aspectRatio`). These should use variables or StyleSheet-defined styles instead of being constructed inline in the component body.

Move this to a StyleUtils helper or use `StyleUtils.getWidthStyle()` / `StyleUtils.getMaximumWidth()` and define the aspect ratio as a variable or style.

Inline style object `{backgroundColor: theme.hoverComponentBG}` should not be used directly in JSX. Use `StyleUtils.getBackgroundColorStyle(theme.hoverComponentBG)` or define this in the StyleSheet.

Replace with:
```tsx
<View style={[styles.mh5, styles.pv2, styles.ph3, StyleUtils.getBackgroundColorStyle(theme.hoverComponentBG), rowIndex === 0 ? styles.borderBottom : styles.borderTop]}>
```

Inline style object `{maxWidth: '100%'}` should not be used directly in JSX. Use a themed style or add this to the StyleSheet.

Replace the inline style with a predefined style, for example:
```tsx
// Use styles.mw100 or add a new style if one doesn't exist
<View style={[shouldUseNarrowLayout ? styles.workspaceSectionMobile : styles.workspaceSection, activeTab !== RULES_TAB.GENERAL && [styles.flex1, styles.mw100]]}>
```

The hardcoded string `'money-request/tax-amount'` duplicates a portion of the route path defined in `DYNAMIC_ROUTES.MONEY_REQUEST_STEP_TAX_AMOUNT.path`. If the path ever changes, this check will silently break.

Use the constant instead:
```tsx
const isTaxAmountForm = Navigation.getActiveRouteWithoutParams().includes(DYNAMIC_ROUTES.MONEY_REQUEST_STEP_TAX_AMOUNT.path.split('/:')[0]);
```
Or extract a constant like `const TAX_AMOUNT_PATH_PREFIX = 'money-request/tax-amount'` to make the relationship explicit.

The inline style `{gap: 20}` uses a magic number. The codebase already defines `gap5` in `src/styles/utils/spacing.ts` which resolves to `{gap: 20}`.

Replace with the existing style constant:
```tsx
innerContainerStyle={styles.gap5}
```

The hex values `'#f7f2ef'` (line 18) and `'#73857e'` (line 21) are hardcoded magic strings without named constants or inline comments explaining what they represent. The other entries in the map use named constants from `colors` (e.g., `colors.productLight200`, `colors.productLight900`), which makes these two raw hex values inconsistent.

Define named constants or add inline comments explaining what these colors represent. Ideally, if these correspond to known product colors, use the appropriate constant from `@styles/theme/colors`:

```ts
// If these are known product colors, add them to the colors module, or at minimum document them:
const CHART_CARD_BG_LIGHT = '#f7f2ef'; // Light-mode chart card background
const CHART_TEXT_SUPPORTING_LIGHT = '#73857e'; // Light-mode chart supporting text
```

The hardcoded string `'Unknown Submitter'` is a user-facing fallback that should use a translation key instead of an inline English string. The rest of the codebase uses `translate('common.hidden')` or similar translation keys for display name fallbacks.

Replace the magic string with a proper translation key, for example:
```tsx
multiPersonalDetailsSelector(submittersAccountIDs)(personalDetailsList)?.map(({displayName, login}) => displayName ?? login ?? translate('common.hidden'));
```
Note: this will require passing `translate` into the selector or restructuring to perform the mapping outside the selector.

The hardcoded fallback rate `67` (cents per mile) is a magic number. It should be extracted to a named constant for clarity and maintainability.

Define a constant such as:
```ts
const DEFAULT_P2P_RATE_CENTS_PER_MILE = 67;
```
and use it in the fallback:
```ts
const p2pRate: DefaultP2PMileageRate = defaultRate ?? {rate: DEFAULT_P2P_RATE_CENTS_PER_MILE, unit: CONST.CUSTOM_UNITS.DISTANCE_UNIT_MILES};
```

The string `'fetch'` is a magic value representing the NitroFetch target identifier. It appears here at `clearTokenRefresh('fetch')` and again at line 54 as `target: 'fetch'`, as well as in `src/libs/actions/Session/index.ts`. This identifier should be a named constant to improve readability and maintainability.

Extract it to a constant:
```ts
const NITRO_FETCH_TARGET = 'fetch' as const;
```
Then reference it in both `clearTokenRefresh(NITRO_FETCH_TARGET)` and `target: NITRO_FETCH_TARGET`.

The string `'fetch'` is a magic value representing the NitroFetch target identifier. It is used here and also in `src/libs/registerPrefetchTokenRefresh/index.native.ts` (lines 46 and 54) without being defined as a named constant. If the library changes this identifier or if it needs to be referenced in more places, every occurrence must be found and updated manually.

Extract it to a shared constant, for example:
```ts
// In a shared location, e.g., src/libs/registerPrefetchTokenRefresh/constants.ts
export const NITRO_FETCH_TARGET = 'fetch' as const;
```
Then use `NITRO_FETCH_TARGET` in both `Session/index.ts` and `registerPrefetchTokenRefresh/index.native.ts`.

`duration: 300` is a magic number repeated across `GroupChildrenContainer.tsx` and `GroupHeader.tsx`. This animation duration should be extracted to a named constant.

Define a shared constant and reuse it:
```tsx
const EXPAND_COLLAPSE_ANIMATION_DURATION = 300;

withTiming(target, {duration: EXPAND_COLLAPSE_ANIMATION_DURATION, easing}, ...)
```

The hardcoded string `` `search/view/${parentReportID}` `` is a magic value that duplicates the route path defined in `DYNAMIC_ROUTES.SEARCH_REPORT_VIEW`. If the route path changes, this check will silently break.

Use the route definition instead:

```ts
activeRoute.includes(DYNAMIC_ROUTES.SEARCH_REPORT_VIEW.getRoute(parentReportID))
```

The hardcoded string `` `search/view/${reportID}` `` is a magic value that duplicates the route path defined in `DYNAMIC_ROUTES.SEARCH_REPORT_VIEW`. If the route path changes, this check will silently break.

The hardcoded string `` `search/view/${chatReportID}` `` is a magic value that duplicates the route path defined in `DYNAMIC_ROUTES.SEARCH_REPORT_VIEW`. If the route path changes, this check will silently break.

```ts
check: (activeRoute: string) => activeRoute.includes(DYNAMIC_ROUTES.SEARCH_REPORT_VIEW.getRoute(chatReportID)),
```

The values `40` for `height` and `width` in `avatarAgentApprover` are magic numbers. There is already a named constant `variables.avatarSizeNormal` (which equals `40`) that conveys the semantic intent.

Use the named constant instead:
```ts
avatarAgentApprover: {
    backgroundColor: theme.icon,
    borderRadius: variables.componentBorderRadiusCircle,
    height: variables.avatarSizeNormal,
    width: variables.avatarSizeNormal,
},
```

The regex pattern `/^mcp-([a-z0-9]+)-/` is a magic string that encodes knowledge about the MCP OAuth `partnerUserID` format without being defined as a named constant. If this format is referenced elsewhere or changes in the future, a named constant makes the intent clearer and the pattern easier to find and update.

Define the regex as a named constant alongside the other MCP-related constants:

```ts
const MCP_PARTNER_USER_ID_PATTERN = /^mcp-([a-z0-9]+)-/;
```

Then use it in `getDeviceDisplayName`:

```ts
const mcpMatch = login.partnerUserID ? MCP_PARTNER_USER_ID_PATTERN.exec(login.partnerUserID) : null;
```

The magic number `100000` is used as an upper bound for valid Excel serial date numbers without being defined as a named constant. Since this file is a new shared utility, consider extracting it to improve readability.

Suggested fix:

```ts
// Excel serial date 100000 corresponds to ~2173-10-14, well beyond any reasonable CSV date
const MAX_EXCEL_SERIAL_DATE = 100000;
```

Then use `inputInt < MAX_EXCEL_SERIAL_DATE` in the condition.

The translation key `'domain.members.membersFeatureList.title'` does not exist in `src/languages/en.ts`. The PR's `en.ts` diff adds `membersFeatureList.subtitle`, `membersFeatureList.controlPolicyCreation`, `membersFeatureList.enableSamlSso`, and `membersFeatureList.enforce2FA`, but there is no `title` key. This will cause a runtime issue where the FeatureList title displays the raw translation path string instead of a user-facing title. Add the missing `title` key to `membersFeatureList` in `src/languages/en.ts`: ```ts membersFeatureList: { title: 'Domain members', // or whatever the intended title is subtitle: ({domainName}: {domainName: string}) => `Verify your domain for more control over ${domainName} members in Expensify.`, controlPolicyCreation: 'Restrict workspace creation', enableSamlSso: 'Enable SAML SSO', enforce2FA: 'Enforce 2FA', }, ```

The string literal `'USD'` is used as a fallback currency code, but the constant `CONST.CURRENCY.USD` is already available and imported in this file (line 9). Using the named constant improves readability and ensures consistency if the default currency value ever changes.

Replace the magic string with the existing constant:
```tsx
const currency = sanitizeCurrencyCode(firstItem?.currency ?? CONST.CURRENCY.USD);
```

The hardcoded value `32` for the skeleton content loader height is a magic number, also duplicated in `TableRow.tsx`. It should be extracted to a named constant or added to `src/styles/variables.ts`.

Use a shared constant such as `variables.tableSkeletonContentHeight` instead of the hardcoded `32`.

The hardcoded value `32` for the skeleton content loader height is a magic number that also appears in `TableSkeleton.tsx`. It should be extracted to a named constant or added to `src/styles/variables.ts` for clarity and consistency.

Extract to a shared constant, e.g.:
```ts
// in variables.ts
tableSkeletonContentHeight: 32,
```
